newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX index resumes climb.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX index resumes climb.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mostly higher on Monday pushing the BUX index into record territory as Wall Street's rise last Friday showed the way, traders said.
"Everything is pegged to the U.S. market," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft. "If they rise, we follow them."
The BUX index, which suffered a 10-point correction on Friday after a 17-session rising string, finished at 4,742.70 points, up 28.20.

The pace of rise has slowed from last week's overheated market, when the daily gain of the index averaged well over 100 points, but turnover remained strong, reflecting new funds coming onto the market, traders said.
"Quite a number of investors opened new positions on Hungary," Stalmayer said.
Domestic small investors, usually little more than bystanders, have also increased their activity, he added.
Traders said oil and gas company MOL triggered the most attention after newspaper reports said that U.S. oil company Teneco had made an offer for the yet-to-be-privatised state-owned stake in MOL.
As a result of the offer Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt will review whether a change in MOL's privatisation strategy is necessary, the report said.
MOL shares hit a new record high of 2,750 forints but later slipped back to end at 2,680, up 80.
Another stock reaching a new high was tile manufacturer Zalakeramia which peaked at a new record of 8,150 forints. It closed at 8,150, up 500.
Zalakeramia said today it would hold an extraordinary general meeting on February 12 to discuss planned new acquisitions.
Traders were optimistic about the market's outlook.
"There seems to be (ample) supply of money and this looks like lasting a while," Stalmayer said, adding that annual results to be published soon might also give a fresh boost to the bourse."
Companies have to release their preliminary 1996 results by February 15.
